d.g: The weight or mass of an organism.
a nuclear reactor that uses water as a coolant and moderator;  the water boils in the reactor core and the steam produced can drive a steam turbine

d.x: It is Jim C.’s custom always to say “Up Simba” in a fake-deep bwana voice as he hefts the camera to his right shoulder […]

bwana.e: Borrowed from Swahili bwana (“master”), from Arabic أَبُونَا (ʔabūnā, “our father”). Doublet of abbot.

d.x: When I got home I called in the bwthyn where our welter-weight, Wil Shon Morgan, lived.

bwthyn.e: Unadapted borrowing from Welsh bwthyn. Possibly cognate with Scottish Gaelic bothag, Scots and Scottish English bothy.
